tool_input.command:
t=$(mktemp -d); cd "$t"
# rotate: 5 archives, keep 2 -> the 3 oldest go, the 2 newest stay, sidecar follows archive
mkdir -p d
for s in 20260101-000000 20260102-000000 20260103-000000 20260104-000000 20260105-000000; do
  : > "d/app-$s.tar.gz"; : > "d/app-$s.tar.gz.sha256"
done
out=$(bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/soakfp36-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest d --name app --keep 2)
echo "$out"
echo "remaining: $(ls d | tr '\n' ' ')"
# dry-run with --keep=1 form on the 2 remaining
bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/soakfp36-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest=d --name=app --keep=1 -n
echo "after dry-run: $(ls d | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files"
# keep must stay >=1
bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/soakfp36-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest d --name app --keep 0; echo "keep0 rc=$?"
bash /Users/vitor/.cache/flashnext-concurrency/claude-work/soakfp36-d/rotate.sh --quiet --dest d --name app --keep x 2>&1 | tail -1; echo "keepx rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
rm -rf "$t"
tool_input.description: Smoke-test rotate.sh oldest-first deletion, dry-run, and --keep validation
Show changed files and run test suite once more

result:
All done — `bash tests/run_tests.sh` passes all 8 tests.

What changed:

- **rotate.sh** — the surplus calculation was `tail -n +"$keep"` on an ascending (oldest-first) list, which deleted from the *keep*-th line through the end (including the newest) whenever `total >= keep`. Now the surplus is the first `total - keep` lines (`head -n`, guarded against BSD `head`'s rejection of `0`), so with exactly N archives nothing is deleted and rotation removes the oldest first. Sidecars still go with their archives; `--keep 0`/non-integer `--keep` are still refused.
- **verify.sh** — sidecar parsing used `awk '{print $2}'`, truncating file names at the first space, so `my backup-…tar.gz` looked "archive missing". It now takes the digest as the text before the first space and the name as everything after the shasum `<digest>␣␣` separator (a sidecar line with no separator is still "malformed sidecar"), and the digest comparison uses a quoted `[[ ]]`. Genuine mismatches still report BAD/exit 2.
- **lib/common.sh** (new) — the shared option-parsing block (`--dest`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q/--quiet`, `-n/--dry-run`, `-h/--help`, `--`, positionals into `ARGS`, `is_uint`/`need_value` + `--keep` validation) and `resolve_dir`, with a double-source guard like `lib/log.sh`.
- **rotate.sh** and **verify.sh** source `lib/common.sh` in place of their inline copies (defining `usage`/`parse_local_option` first, as the parser calls them); `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` are untouched.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — two new tests next to the existing ones: verify reports ok (exit 0) for a space-containing archive name, and rotate with exactly N archives and `--keep N` deletes nothing (newest present).

I changed `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh` and `tests/run_tests.sh`, and added `lib/common.sh`. (One leftover: the smoke-test script at `/tmp/bk-smoke/smoke.sh` — deletion needed approval, so I left it.)
